title: Cloudflare Details Its Migration from WordPress to EmDash
gist: Cloudflare moved its main blog from WordPress to EmDash, its in-house open-source TypeScript CMS, running on Workers with KV/Workers Cache, and on Hyperdrive to PlanetScale. It reports flat p95 latency, capacity tested to 7,000 RPS, and a proxy-Worker cutover from 1% to 100% of traffic in one day. EmDash is still pre-v1, and the move shows Cloudflare pulling CMS workloads onto its developer platform.

insights.claim: Cloudflare migrated its main corporate blog off WordPress onto EmDash, its own internally developed open-source TypeScript CMS positioned as a WordPress successor, acting as 'Customer Zero' for the product.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Cloudflare is using its own flagship property to validate a WordPress replacement that pulls CMS workloads onto its Workers platform; watch EmDash adoption as a new NET developer-platform funnel and a competitive threat to the WordPress ecosystem (Automattic, WP hosts).
insights.locator: The company describes itself as "Customer Zero"

insights.claim: EmDash was released as a v0.1.0 developer preview in April 2026 and, after Cloudflare's own migration surfaced editor-experience and scheduled-post issues, the team is working toward a v1 release with no official date announced.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Product is still pre-1.0; enterprise CMS switching from WordPress is unlikely at scale until v1 ships, so treat near-term revenue impact as optionality rather than a driver.
insights.locator: According to the article, editors encountered

insights.claim: A Reddit user comparing EmDash with Ghost claims EmDash is much cheaper, far more AI-interactive and near-infinitely extensible, signalling early developer enthusiasm for it as an alternative to incumbent headless/blog CMSs.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Anecdotal community sentiment only; a useful early indicator to track for EmDash traction versus Ghost/WordPress, but not evidence of adoption.
insights.quote: EmDash's cost is much less and the AI interactivity is much greater.

insights.claim: Cloudflare's production EmDash deployment runs on a Worker with layered caching (Workers Cache plus an EmDash object cache on Workers KV) and connects to a PlanetScale database through Cloudflare Hyperdrive.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: The reference architecture bundles several paid Cloudflare developer-platform products (Workers, KV, Hyperdrive) into one CMS deployment, so each EmDash adopter consumes multiple NET services and creates stickiness; PlanetScale gains as the partnered database.

insights.claim: Moving a CMS from a traditional WordPress stack to a serverless edge runtime shifts the workload from generic hosting onto a single vendor's compute, cache and database-connectivity layer, making the edge vendor the platform rather than just the CDN.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Supports the thesis that Cloudflare is converting CDN customers into application-platform customers with higher ARPU and switching costs; watch developer-platform revenue disclosures.

insights.claim: The Cloudflare blog normally serves about 75 requests per second with spikes above 5,000 RPS, and the new EmDash platform was load-tested to handle up to 7,000 RPS.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Spiky, cache-friendly publishing workloads are where edge caching gives the biggest advantage over origin-hosted WordPress, and that is the segment EmDash is best placed to win.

insights.claim: Cloudflare reports that p95 response latency on EmDash stays flat and consistent under load, while the previous WordPress platform showed periodic latency spikes.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: A vendor-reported benchmark that Cloudflare will likely use in marketing against WordPress hosting; take it with the bias of self-reporting in mind.
insights.quote: the new system maintains a remarkably flat, consistent response profile

insights.claim: Cloudflare moved traffic from WordPress to EmDash with a proxy Worker that set a version cookie for routing and fell back per request to the legacy blog on any 500 error, starting at 1% of traffic and reaching 100% within a single day.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Cheap, low-risk cutover patterns that run on the edge vendor's own platform lower the cost of leaving incumbent platforms, which speeds up displacement of legacy hosting.

insights.claim: Practitioners note that a safe platform cutover needs a kill switch, per-request fallback and metrics split by cohort, so that cache regressions are caught before a 1% rollout becomes 100%.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: A reusable checklist for judging migration risk in any infrastructure switch; vendors that ship these primitives natively reduce buyers' switching friction.
insights.quote: A good rollout plan usually needs a kill switch, per-request fallback, and metrics split by cohort

insights.claim: As part of the migration, Cloudflare launched an MCP server for the Cloudflare Blog and another for EmDash that lets authors browse, create, edit, publish and schedule content through AI agents.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Agent-native CMS tooling is an emerging point of difference against WordPress; it reflects a wider move to make content systems operable by agents, a trend Cloudflare is betting on across its product line.
